Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout throughput collapse — experiencing 10x latency and failures

Hannah,

We started seeing a severe degradation in checkout throughput at ~14:45 EDT. Successful checkouts dropped from ~120/s to under 6/s over a 7 minute window; frontend shows constant streaming stalls and a spike in 502/timeout errors from the Redwood SDK. Latency to the generation endpoint is up to 18s for token streaming — this is blocking our holiday promo.

I attached a pcap and a short HAR for your infra team (capture-20280322.pcap). We also see repeated client-side logs showing \"truncated header\" and \"failed dechunk\" messages right before the drop.

Can you triage and confirm if this is on your side or something in our edge/proxy? This is impacting revenue — we need a root cause and ETA.

-Natalie

Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Checkout throughput collapse — initial triage

Thanks for the ping and the pcap, Hannah. I started a local replay against our streaming parser. Initial observations: the customer pcap shows header lines split across TCP frames in an unusual way — sometimes mid-token — and our client dechunker assumes CRLF-aligned boundaries. If headers arrive fragmented (header-name partially in one frame, remainder in next) our parser currently treats that as a malformed header and drops the stream.

Action items I'm starting now:
- Reproduce with a minimal harness to confirm the exact fragment pattern (working on a repro).
- Check SDK versions in their logs (Natalie: which SDK version and edge region are you on?).
- Provide a short-term mitigation (option to disable streaming dechunking or fall back to non-streaming endpoint).

Estimate: if this is purely parser logic, I can get a PR with a guard and tests within 3-4 hours; hotfix build to QA in ~6 hours. If it's a protocol mismatch in their proxy, mitigation via routing may be faster (1 hour).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 17:05:33 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: Checkout throughput collapse — root cause & workaround

I reproduced the failure pattern in staging with tcp-replay of the customer's pcap. Root cause: our client-side HTTP streaming dechunker fails when header continuations are split such that a header value token is separated from its name by TCP reassembly boundaries plus an intermediate proxy inserting a small keepalive chunk. The parser's state machine expects header-name + ':' in the same buffer slice. When split, we treat it as an invalid header and close the stream.

I pushed a branch: fix/dechunk-headers-20280322 (contains a defensive reassembly pass that buffers partial header tokens up to 2KB and retries header parse). Quick notes:
- Added unit + integration tests reproducing split-boundary case.
- Patch is backward-compatible; negligible perf impact for typical traffic.

Attachments: log-snippet.txt (contains failing and post-patch traces).

Immediate mitigation (recommended):
1) Customer side: set SDK config streaming_dechunk=false (falls back to non-chunked handling) — we can provide a config patch and a small client-side flag.
2) Platform-side: route traffic to a different edge cluster (us-west) where their proxy chain doesn't insert the keepalive chunk.

I can produce a hotfix build within 4 hours and coordinate a staged rollout. If Hannah approves, I'll cut the build and notify QA.

-Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Urgent: Checkout throughput collapse — planned actions + ETA

Natalie — thanks for the pcap and patience. Quick summary and plan:

What we found: our client SDK parser can mis-handle header fragments produced by certain proxy chains (your pcap shows the keepalive chunk pattern). This results in streams being closed and a sharp drop in throughput.

Short-term mitigations (please choose one so we can move immediately):
- Option A (fastest): We provide a config you can toggle (streaming_dechunk=false) that will avoid the streaming dechunker and should return you to normal throughput within minutes. We will send the patch instructions (workaround_instructions.md).
- Option B: Route a fraction of traffic to our us-west edge cluster; Sean has validated this avoids the proxy keepalive pattern and will reduce risk while we roll a hotfix (we can help with a temporary route change).

Hotfix ETA: engineering expects to have a tested hotfix build in 4 hours and a staged rollout ready in ~6 hours from now. We'll coordinate a QA window and confirm the build IDs. If you'd like, we can perform the rollout during a short maintenance window overnight.

Compensation: If the impact is >30 minutes we will evaluate a service credit; I'll confirm with billing/legal and follow up.

Attached: workaround_instructions.md (small client patch and toggles). I'll follow up with the hotfix build ID and release notes.

Apologies again for the disruption. We'll keep you posted every 30 minutes until resolved.

—Hannah
